reply_text:
I found five dated, forward-looking AI statements Pichai made in 2018, including the one you already have. All are short-range product launch promises. I found nothing in 2018 that puts a date on AGI or on what AI will be able to do over the long term.

**What I found**
- **Google I/O keynote, 8 May 2018** (third-party transcript on singjupost.com, Pichai's sections only). Pichai himself made four dated promises there:
  - **Smart Compose:** coming to all Gmail users "this month".
  - **Google Photos:** AI features rolling out "in the next couple of months".
  - **Duplex:** the business-hours calls rolling out "as an experiment in the coming weeks".
  - **John Legend's voice:** coming "later this year". This is your recorded file.
- **"Coming weeks" is borderline.** I kept the Duplex line because it names a short span, but you may decide it's too vague, closer to "soon".
- **Speaker check.** The same keynote's promise of "30 languages… by the end of this year" for the Assistant came from Scott Huffman, and the "this summer" launch dates came from Lilian Rincon. I left both out.
- **Q2 2018 earnings call, 23 July** (Motley Fool transcript). In his prepared remarks Pichai said the Assistant would be in more than 30 languages and 80 countries by the end of the year. At the Q3 call he reported 20 languages and 76 countries. That is a count from October, not a year-end result.

**Checked, nothing dated**
- **Washington Post interview, December:** he said AI fears are "very legitimate". His only time words were "mid- to long term", which is not about AGI. The article says he "vowed to address in the coming year" YouTube content problems, but that is the reporter's paraphrase and not about AI.
- **Axios interview, December:** no dated statements.
- **Q3 2018 earnings call:** Duplex for Pixel users, with no date given.
- **Recode/MSNBC "Revolution" town hall, January** (the "electricity or fire" remark): search results showed only news coverage, with no dated predictions.

**Gaps**
- The first fixed search's results printed only partly because of a parsing error in my code. I recovered them from the saved results and did not run it again.
- I did not open the AI principles post (June), the Q1 2018 call, or the Q4 2017 call held on 1 February 2018. That last one counts as 2018 and is still unchecked.
- Seeking Alpha was never fetched.
- I used all 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings.
